monotonicity_and_sign_lemmas.L5: Psi_w = -(2w sin b + b sin 2w) < 0 for 0 < w <= W and 0 < b < pi, so Psi is strictly decreasing in w on [0,W].
monotonicity_and_sign_lemmas.L6: Om = b cos(w+b/2) cos(w-b/2); for |w| <= W both arguments lie in [b-pi/2, pi/2] subset [-pi/2,pi/2], hence Om >= 0 with equality exactly at |w| = W.
monotonicity_and_sign_lemmas.L7: for b > pi/2, D := -Phi_w = b sin 2w - 2w sin b satisfies D(0)=0, D_ww = -4b sin 2w <= 0 (concave on 0<=2w<=pi-b) and D(W) = (2b-pi) sin b > 0, hence D(w) >= (w/W) D(W) > 0: Phi is strictly decreasing in w on [0,W].
monotonicity_and_sign_lemmas.L8: for 0 < b < pi/2, Phi > 0 on [0,W].  For w in [b/2,W], Phi = Q+Om with Q,Om >= 0 and never both zero.  For w in [0,b/2] put p = b/2+w, q = b/2-w >= 0, p+q = b <= pi/2; then Phi = (p+q)cos p cos q - pq sin(p+q) and, dividing by cos p cos q > 0, the claim is p+q > pq(tan p + tan q). Since q <= pi/2-p one has pq tan p <= p(pi/2-p)tan p < p, the last step being (pi/2-p)tan p < 1, i.e. s < tan s at s = pi/2-p; symmetrically pq tan q < q.  Adding gives the claim strictly unless p=q=0.

bstar.uniqueness: f'(b) = -sin(b/2) - (b/4) cos(b/2) certified strictly negative on [1.70,1.75], and f(1.70) > 0 > f(1.75)

w_Dottie.role: limit position of the Wpot roots at beta -> 0 and beta -> pi:  t = pi/2 +- w_D

c.role: the y-limits of both curves at beta = pi/2: the torque lens tends to y = c-1 and y = -c, the potential curve to y = 1-c and y = c

exact_linear_relation: Wtau(beta,t) + Wpot(beta,t) = 2*Wwgt(beta,t) identically -- the three determinants span a 2-dimensional space (proved symbolically in validate.py, sympy)

beta = 0.statement: t - beta = t, so Wtau = Wpot = Wwgt = 0 identically in t; the entire column beta = 0 belongs to all three zero sets.

beta = beta*_1.nature: double root of the torque Wronskian (lens endpoint)
beta = beta*_1.why: Phi(pi-beta,0) = 0 and Phi_w(b,0) = 0 identically, so w = 0 is a double root; the Wtau count jumps 0 -> 2 here.

beta = pi/2.statement: b = pi/2 on BOTH pieces and W = pi/4.  Phi(pi/2,pi/4) = Psi(pi/2,pi/4) = Om(pi/2,pi/4) = 0 and Phi_w(pi/2,pi/4) = 0, so all three determinants vanish exactly on the same set {t = 0, t = pi/2} (mod pi) -- both points lying ON the kink lattice -- and there is no interior root (L5/L7 with Phi(.,0), Psi(.,0) > 0).
beta = pi/2.mass_direction: at both roots h(t) = h(t-beta) = 0, so the mass direction is 0/0; the curves extend by the limits y = c-1, -c (torque) and y = 1-c, c (potential).

beta = beta*_2.nature: double root of the torque Wronskian (lens endpoint)
beta = beta*_2.why: Phi(beta,0) = 0 and Phi_w(b,0) = 0 identically; the Wtau count jumps 2 -> 0 here.

beta = pi.nature: degenerate column (identified with beta = 0 by pi-periodicity)
beta = pi.statement: t - beta = t (mod pi); all three determinants vanish identically.

torque_lens.certified_boxes_sample_note: evenly spaced sample of the 205666 certified boxes; the summary numbers above are computed over all of them.  The complete list is in certificate_full.json.gz

potential_curve.certified_boxes_sample_note: evenly spaced sample of the 508300 certified boxes; the summary numbers above are computed over all of them.  The complete list is in certificate_full.json.gz

weight_wronskian_image.statement: for every beta in (0,pi) the zero set of Wwgt in t is exactly {0, beta} (mod pi); at t = 0 one has h(t) = 0 so s1 = 0 and y = 0, at t = beta one has h(t-beta) = 0 so s0 = 0 and y = +1 (= -1).  The image is therefore exactly the two horizontal lines y = 0 and y = +1.
weight_wronskian_image.certified_by: L6 (Om = b cos(w+b/2) cos(w-b/2), both cosine arguments in [-pi/2,pi/2], vanishing only at |w| = W)
weight_wronskian_image.per_beta_table_evidence: every row of per_beta_table has Wwgt with n_interior_roots = 0 and exactly two kink roots t = 0 and t = beta (mod pi)

pieces_1D.name: torque Wronskian lens, upper branch
pieces_1D.equation: Wtau(beta,t) = 0, the root whose mass ratio has rho > 1 (y > -1/2)
pieces_1D.parameterisation: the two roots are w = +-w_r(beta) with w_r the unique zero of Phi(b,.) in (0,(pi-b)/2); on piece B (beta < pi/2, b = pi-beta, t = beta/2 + w) this branch is w = +w_r, on piece A (beta > pi/2, b = beta, t = (beta+pi)/2 + w) it is w = -w_r
pieces_1D.note: y = -1/2 exactly at the two endpoints beta*_1, beta*_2; y -> -c as beta -> pi/2 (limit, not attained)

pieces_1D.name: torque Wronskian lens, lower branch
pieces_1D.parameterisation: exact mirror of 1D-1 under t -> beta - t (mod pi), which sends the mass ratio rho to 1/rho and hence y to -1-y

pieces_1D.name: potential Wronskian curve, lower branch
pieces_1D.parameterisation: the two roots are w = +-w_r(beta) with w_r the unique zero of Psi(b,.) in (0,(pi-b)/2); piece A for beta < pi/2 (b = beta, t = (beta+pi)/2 + w, this branch is w = -w_r), piece B for beta > pi/2 (b = pi-beta, t = beta/2 + w, this branch is w = +w_r)
pieces_1D.y_range: ( c , 1/2 )  -- entirely inside the MIXED-sign sector y > 0

pieces_1D.name: potential Wronskian curve, upper branch
pieces_1D.parameterisation: mirror of 1D-3 under t -> beta - t (mod pi); y -> 1-y

pieces_1D.name: weight Wronskian image, root t = 0 (mod pi)
pieces_1D.equation: Wwgt(beta,t) = 0 at t = 0; there h(t) = 0, so s1 = 0
pieces_1D.note: coincides with the degenerate stratum 1D-9 (second teacher massless).  Here s1 = h(0) = 0 exactly and s0 != 0, so atan2 gives +-pi/2 and the fold gives y = 0; the per-beta table reports an enclosure of width < 1e-27 around 0.

pieces_1D.name: weight Wronskian image, root t = beta (mod pi)
pieces_1D.equation: Wwgt(beta,t) = 0 at t = beta; there h(t-beta) = 0, so s0 = 0
pieces_1D.image_in_map: the horizontal line y = +1 (identified with y = -1)
pieces_1D.note: coincides with the degenerate stratum 1D-10.  In the per-beta table the y field of this root is reported as null: s0 = -h(0) = 0 EXACTLY, so atan2(s0,s1) sits on the seam of the (-,-) fold and the interval routine correctly declines to pick a branch.  The value y = +1 follows from the exact vanishing of s0 together with ratioCoord's convention a <= 0 -> a + pi, not from a numerical evaluation.

pieces_1D.name: degenerate column beta = 0
pieces_1D.content: all three determinants vanish identically in t; coincident teacher directions

pieces_1D.name: degenerate column beta = pi/2 (orthogonal teacher)
pieces_1D.content: all three determinants have the SAME zero set {t = 0, t = pi/2} (mod pi), both on the kink lattice; the mass direction degenerates to 0/0 at both

pieces_1D.name: degenerate stratum y = 0
pieces_1D.equation: s1 = 0 -- the second teacher atom is massless

pieces_1D.name: degenerate stratum y = +1 (= y = -1)
pieces_1D.equation: s0 = 0 -- the first teacher atom is massless; psi = 0 and psi = pi are the same projective line, so the top and bottom edges of the box are one stratum

pieces_1D.name: degenerate column beta = pi
pieces_1D.content: identified with beta = 0 by the pi-periodicity of the centered kernel; all three determinants vanish identically

pieces_0D.name: left lens endpoint / torque double root
pieces_0D.why: double root of Wtau at t = beta/2 (w = 0): Phi(pi-beta,0) = 0 and Phi_w(.,0) = 0.  The Wtau root count jumps 0 -> 2.  Meeting point of 1D-1 and 1D-2.  beta*_1 = 2u* with tan u* = pi/2 - u*.

pieces_0D.name: right lens endpoint / torque double root
pieces_0D.why: double root of Wtau at t = (beta+pi)/2 (w = 0).  Count jumps 2 -> 0.  beta*_2 = pi - beta*_1 = b*, (b*/2) tan(b*/2) = 1.

pieces_0D.name: torque lens meets the column beta = pi/2 (upper)
pieces_0D.why: the Wtau root reaches the kink t = beta (equivalently t = 0); the mass direction is 0/0 there and the curve extends by the limit y = -c, c = (2/pi) arctan(2/pi).  y-extremum of 1D-1.

pieces_0D.name: torque lens meets the column beta = pi/2 (lower)
pieces_0D.why: mirror of 0D-3 under y -> -1-y; y-extremum of 1D-2.

pieces_0D.name: potential curve meets the column beta = pi/2 (lower)
pieces_0D.why: the Wpot root reaches the kink lattice; limit y = c.  y-extremum of 1D-3.

pieces_0D.name: potential curve meets the column beta = pi/2 (upper)
potential curve endpoint on the column beta = 0
pieces_0D.why: as beta -> 0 the two Wpot roots tend to t = pi/2 +- w_D with w_D the Dottie number (cos w = w), and the mass ratio tends to rho = -1, i.e. y = 1/2.  1D-3 and 1D-4 meet here.

pieces_0D.name: potential curve endpoint on the column beta = pi
pieces_0D.why: mirror of 0D-7 under beta -> pi - beta.

pieces_0D.name: beta = 0 meets y = 0
pieces_0D.why: corner of the degenerate strata 1D-7 and 1D-9 (also the endpoint of the weight-Wronskian image 1D-5)

pieces_0D.name: beta = pi/2 meets y = 0
pieces_0D.why: crossing of the degenerate column 1D-8 with 1D-9/1D-5

non_intersections: The torque lens (1D-1/1D-2) and the potential curve (1D-3/1D-4) never meet in the map: a common zero of Wtau and Wpot forces Q = Om = 0, and Om = 0 only at |w| = W, where Q = (pi/4)(pi-2b) sin b, so b = pi/2, i.e. beta = pi/2 and t in {0, pi/2}.  At that (beta,t) the mass direction is 0/0 and the two curves approach DIFFERENT limits (y = -c, c-1 versus y = c, 1-c), so their images are disjoint.
The torque lens stays inside y in (c-1, -c) subset (-1,0), hence never meets y = 0 or y = +-1.
The potential curve stays inside y in (c, 1-c) subset (0,1), hence never meets y = 0 or y = +-1.

a_widgets_mirror.note: reference values produced by ref_widgets.js: node evaluating the literal function sources of website/widgets.js (PI, mod, phiC, HC, dHC, slopeAtom), extracted by identifier with a guard that asserts each extracted function still contains the expected expression

a2_libm.statement: V8's Math.sin/Math.cos and glibc's differ by up to max_abs_sin_cos_difference_node_vs_glibc; feeding node's OWN sin/cos into the Python formulas reproduces every kernel quantity to max_abs_deviation_when_fed_nodes_own_sin_cos, so the reimplementation is formula-identical to the widget.

b_hprime_eq_slopeAtom.method: central difference, mpmath prec=300, step 1e-25, kink lattice avoided by 1e-3

c_reduction_identity.statement: on every sample the interval enclosure of (folded mirror - reduced form) contains 0
